gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the UGREEN's 48,000 mAh is counted at 3.2 V (LiFePO4) while a 40,000 mAh lithium-ion bank is counted at 3.6 V, so 20% more mAh is only about 7% more energy (153.6 Wh vs 144 Wh) for about 45% more weight.
standout_why: Compared against powerbanks.fyi (cited), Macworld's roundup and its UGREEN 48000 review, best-batteries.com and solargenadvisor.com; Tom's Guide (cited) returned only navigation text, so its body is unchecked. powerbanks.fyi lists 153.6 Wh and 144 Wh side by side with no explanation. Macworld gives 153.6 Wh and the generic 'Ah x V = Wh' but no cell voltage or chemistry. best-batteries.com calls the UGREEN LiFePO4 but draws no capacity consequence. solargenadvisor.com says mAh is quoted 'at the cell voltage, usually 3.6 to 3.7V' and covers the 5 A / 240 W cable rule, but lists no bank of 40,000 mAh or more. So rivals hold the pieces; none says the 48,000 figure sits on a lower voltage. The 140 W cable/MagSafe point is already in Macworld and solargenadvisor (standout 0-1 on its own).
decides: Rank this size by maker-stated Wh, not mAh. The UGREEN 48,000 mAh (153.6 Wh, 1,637 g) is roughly a tie on energy with the 40,000 mAh lithium-ion banks (CUKTECH 30: 144 Wh, 1,130 g), not a 20% step up. Its case is then price ($118.99 per the brief; I could not re-read the store today) and three laptop-grade USB-C ports. The 40,000 mAh lithium-ion banks win on weight per Wh. The AOHi Starship's 146 Wh and 916 g are from the brief and Dealectric's record, not re-read today; if they hold, the same logic favours it for anything carried. Secondary: 140 W reaches a 16-inch MacBook Pro only through Apple's MagSafe 3 cable, or a 240 W USB-C cable on Nov 2023 or later models; otherwise plan on 100 W.
